title: Superior Courts Court Dress and Mode of Address Act 1986

sections.shortTitle: Superior Courts Court Dress and Mode of Address Act 1986
sections.description:
Short title and commencement

THE SUPERIOR COURTS (COURT DRESS AND MODE OF ADDRESS) ACT, 1986
THE SUPERIOR COURTS (COURT DRESS
AND MODE OF ADDRESS) ACT, 1986.
(ACT XXVIII OF 1986)
[Dated March
29, 1986]
AN ACT to provide for law
relating to court dress and the mode of address in the Superior Courts.
WHEREAS it is expedient to
provide for law relating to the Court Dress and the Mode of Address in the
Superior Courts, in the manner hereinafter appearing; It is hereby enacted as
follows :‑
1. Short title and
commencement.‑--- (1) This Act may be called the Superior Courts
(Court Dress and Mode of Address) Act, 1986.
(2) It extends to the whole of Azad Jammu and Kashmir
(3) It shall come into force at once.

WHEREAS it is expedient to

2. Definitions.‑ In this Act‑‑‑
(a) "Superior Court"
means the Supreme Court of Azad Jammu and Kashmir, the High Court of Azad Jammu
and Kashmir and the Shariat Court of Azad Jammu and Kashmir;
(b) "Judge" includes
the Chief Justice

Dress of Judge

THE SUPERIOR COURTS (COURT DRESS AND MODE OF ADDRESS) ACT, 1986
THE SUPERIOR COURTS (COURT DRESS
AND MODE OF ADDRESS) ACT, 1986.
(ACT XXVIII OF 1986)
[Dated March
29, 1986]
AN ACT to provide for law
relating to court dress and the mode of address in the Superior Courts.
WHEREAS it is expedient to
provide for law relating to the Court Dress and the Mode of Address in the
Superior Courts, in the manner hereinafter appearing; It is hereby enacted as
follows :‑
3. A Judge of Superior Court shall wear,
while he is attending sittings of the Court, a black sherwani without bands
white shirt, white shalwar or pyijama or a short coat of black material, white
shirt, with turn‑down collar and black tie, white trousers, in the
Summer, and in the Winter, trousers of material in the deeper shades of gray
and a black gown.

sections.shortTitle: Superior Courts Court Dress and Mode of Address Act 1986
sections.description:
Mode of Address

THE SUPERIOR COURTS (COURT DRESS AND MODE OF ADDRESS) ACT, 1986
THE SUPERIOR COURTS (COURT DRESS
AND MODE OF ADDRESS) ACT, 1986.
(ACT XXVIII OF 1986)
[Dated March
29, 1986]
AN ACT to provide for law
relating to court dress and the mode of address in the Superior Courts.
WHEREAS it is expedient to
provide for law relating to the Court Dress and the Mode of Address in the
Superior Courts, in the manner hereinafter appearing; It is hereby enacted as
follows :‑
4. Mode of Address.‑ The use of
the expressions "My Lord" and "Your Lordship" and the like
in relation to a Judge shall be discontinued and he shall only be addressed as
"Sir" or "Janab‑e‑Wala" or "Janab‑e‑Aali"
or referred to in judgements correspondence or other instruments as "Mr.
Justice" so and so or the like.
